title: TWA 3
summary: TWA Flight 3 departed Las Vegas at 19:20 PST on January 16, 1942, bound for Burbank. Fifteen minutes after takeoff at 8,000 feet, the aircraft was 7 miles off course on a compass heading of 218° when it struck Potosi Mountain. The Civil Aeronautics Board determined the navigation error likely resulted from the crew inadvertently using the Boulder City departure course instead of the appropriate Las Vegas outbound course. All 22 aboard perished including actress Carole Lombard.
probable_cause: Navigation error by the captain using compass heading instead of radio navigation. The crew likely confused the Boulder City outbound course of 218° with the Las Vegas course, resulting in the aircraft being flown 7 miles off the designated airway into high terrain.

factors.evidence: the crew was not using radio navigation to follow the airway but was instead using a compass heading of 218°
the plane took off on a clear, moonless night and the airway light beacons had been turned off because of the ongoing Second World War
the crew did not realize the terrain in that direction rose to about 8500 feet while flying at 8000 feet altitude
the flight plan form was completed by the first officer but not signed by the captain, despite a company requirement to do so
the aircraft crashed into a sheer cliff on Potosi Mountain at 7770 feet elevation

events.text: Aircraft took off on a clear, moonless night from Las Vegas Airport bound for Burbank
Flying almost 7 miles off course, the aircraft was at 8000 feet approaching terrain rising to 8500 feet
Crew was using compass heading instead of radio navigation, unaware of terrain threat
Aircraft crashed into a near-vertical cliff on Potosi Mountain at 7770 feet, 32 miles southwest of Las Vegas
